newsitem.title: ITALY: Arms firm in Italian corruption probe denies sales.
newsitem.headline: Arms firm in Italian corruption probe denies sales.

text.p: An Italian arms firm whose managing director has been arrested in a corruption probe said on Monday it had never sold weapons to countries under U.N. embargo.
Newspapers on Sunday published transcripts of wiretaps which investigators believe point to illegal arms trafficking to a number of countries including Iraq and Bosnia.

"As regards the supply of arms to foreign countries under U.N. embargoes, such as Bosnia, the company rules out ever having furnished supplies of any kind," the company, Oto Melara, said in a statement. Oto Melara is a unit of state-owned engineering and aerospace group Finmeccanica .
Its managing director Pier Francesco Guarguaglini was arrested last week in a mounting corruption probe sparked by the arrest on September 15 of the chief of Italy's state railway, Lorenzo Necci.

A judge in the northwest port town of La Spezia on Monday rejected a request by defence lawyers to free the Ferrovie dello Stato managing director, ruling he must remain in jail while the case continues.

Oto Melara said in the statement that the material it produces was for national security. It said its sales were always conducted with the agreement of the Italian and foreign authorities and could not be carried out secretly.
The Italian media have dubbed the case "Tangentopoli (Bribesville) 2" after a corruption scandal which broke in 1992 and toppled Italy's old political guard.
Since Necci's arrest, the probe has mushroomed to include judges, businessmen and lawyers as magistrates look into allegations of trial-fixing and widespread bribery in return for state contracts.
President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro, in a speech on Sunday night in the northern city of Turin, acknowledged that "a serious wound had been re-opened in our country" by the new probe.
But he said magistrates should continue their work and "a scalpel was needed to save the healthy part" of Italy.
